text:
Sending a basket of jasmines to
        a lady

        A jealous portion of your whiteness
is that which today from a green lattice,

        to honor your hand, mine stole,
this one courtly indeed, that one pure.
The
        beautiful dawn among ambers exudes
in its clean cambric a cold substance,

        this one waking earlier than any other day
and its fortune grown greater than
        others.
And
        if you do not know the name of these lush
young ones I offer you
        by the bushel
—who, being so, all look white-haired—

        I will easily believe you can guess it
if among them, Lísida, you mix your
        hands.
If you touch them, you will see they are jasmines.

translation.title: To Marsia, Covering Her Eyes with Her Hand
translation.editorial_note: The translation follows the ornate syntax of the jasmine sonnet while keeping the final tactile reveal.
